summary: Big-O notation describes how the number of steps an algorithm takes grows with the input size n. This program counts steps for O(n), O(log n), and O(n^2) code at three sizes.
notes: steps++ inside each loop counts work directly, so the table is the same on every computer.
When n grows 10 times, linearSearch grows 10 times, binarySearch grows by only about 3 steps, and countPairs grows 100 times.
System.nanoTime() measures real time in nanoseconds, but the numbers change on every run and depend on the machine.
pitfall: Counting steps in an int works here, but countPairs(100000) would need 10 billion steps and overflow int (max about 2.1 billion), printing a negative number. Use long for large counts.
